speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Gout

That diagnosis is incorrect based on your medical history. The presence of pain specifically in the left great toe, combined with worsening activity and a duration of several years, is highly characteristic of gout rather than cellulitis, which is a bacterial skin infection. While I acknowledge your request, I must rely on clinical evidence to provide an accurate diagnosis. Given the classic presentation of the "great toe" and chronic joint involvement, gout is the most likely condition.
